answer: To blunt sybil floods, each new agent must lock a time-decaying bond that matures only after independent peers replay its work trail across epochs. Like yarrow along a river bank, an honest identity stays rooted in one historical channel; a swarm of disposable names cannot take hold, because every claim has to echo prior attested deeds, and a mismatched echo slashes the bond before it unlocks. Identity then costs both capital and a unique, verifiable path.
